newsitem.title: USA: U.S. economy looks very strong--Commerce's Ehrlich.
newsitem.headline: U.S. economy looks very strong--Commerce's Ehrlich.

text.p: The U.S. economy in the first quarter looks "very strong" with consumers going "gangbusters" on spending, a senior official said Thursday.

"What we've seen for the first quarter looks very strong," Commerce Undersecretary Everett Ehrlich told Reuters Financial Television. "If you take a look at the numbers we have so far, the first quarter is moving up from three to four (percent growth) and perhaps beyond," he said.
The Commerce Department reported earlier that retail sales rose 0.8 percent last month after an upwardly revised jump of 1.5 percent in January.
Ehrlich said that growth in the first quarter looks to be in the "broad range" of that of the fourth, when the economy surged ahead at an annualized 3.9 percent pace.
"The consumer sector in the U.S. is going gangbusters right now," he added.
Ehrlich acknowleded that consumer spending may have been boosted by unusually warm winter weather and faster and larger tax refunds, which are up about 20 percent from last year.
But he argued that consumer spending was strong overall, despite the special factors. "We're really seeing strength, I believe, in both the January and February figures," he said.
While consumer spending may have accelerated in the early part of this year, it has been strong for some months now, thanks to growth in both jobs and income, Ehrlich said.
He said the U.S. jobs market looks strong, but added that there is no sign of a rapid pick-up in wages.
"We see continued strength in the labor market but no sign of a change in wages," Ehrlich said, referring to the results of Wednesday's "Beige Book" report on the economy by the Federal Reserve.
